content.text: I'll trace how a due-date issue is selected, checked once, and delivered to the assignee through their chosen channels.

content.thinking: Need to implement listOverdueIssues and trace how emails are sent from notification rows.
The user specified that when a due date passes without anyone looking, the assigned person should be notified once.
I need to understand how the email channel delivers.
Reviewing the scheduler, event registry, and email path for immediate notifications.
Checking whether the email channel sends messages immediately or stores them first.

I am examining webhook listener events and how in-app notifications are listed.

Also checking the emit function and whether listOrgIdsForRollup incorrectly limits organizations. A comment in resolveChannels contradicts its code: it claims digestOnly suppresses immediate email, but the logic actually allows it when digest_email is enabled.

The email channel is likely just a marker. Digest jobs send emails for digestOnly subscribers by reading unread notifications.

The overdue email template exists, but nothing in src calls renderEmail("overdue") except the template switch.

Notifications are delivered through the notification row channels. In-app UI uses listNotifications. Channels resolve from NotificationPreference: inApp, email, or digestOnly. Deduplication uses an in-process Set that is not persisted. The cron job shares this module-level set with direct POST calls. The job skips issues where dueAt is null and checks reported.has(id). It does not call isOverdue() itself; SQL handles dueAt, status, and archived filtering.

The job emits unassigned issues but skips fan-out when assigneeId is null. It announces the overdue state without selecting recipients or channels.

The LIVE_ONLY filter always excludes archived issues because it is an empty object. The actual archive guard lives in listOverdueIssues via livePredicate.

listOrgIdsForRollup batches organizations in groups of 50, which may miss some orgs.

Closed statuses done and canceled are excluded by the open-status array.

The cron route serves as an alternate trigger to the scheduler.

Instrumentation order is register() then registerEventHandlers, which imports notification-service and subscribes registerFanOut, then startScheduler. The scheduler ticks every 60 seconds; overdue issues are processed once per hour, and the first tick always evaluates due items. Each enqueue uses an ID like `overdue-issues:${minute}`.

If emit throws, the issue is not added to reported and retries on the next pass. If emit swallows a rejection via allSettled, the job marks it reported and skips retrying the notification.

The actor is never skipped because the overdue event has no actorId. Recipients are deduplicated with a Set. A null preference defaults to in-app and email. Muting all channels suppresses delivery entirely. digestOnly without the digest_email flag drops the email channel but keeps in-app if set.

Email is stored on the notification row, yet no immediate mailer reads it directly. Digests are built by listing subscribers, gathering unread notifications in the window, rendering the email, and marking them read so they are not resent.

The user's question about "channels they chose" maps to resolveChannels rather than a separate mailer.
I have a solid picture. I will write the explanatory prose.

content.text:
A due issue is announced by a scheduled scan that publishes one `issue.overdue` event. The notification fan-out turns that event into a single row for the assignee, using the channels stored on their preference. The scan itself never sends mail and never picks a person.

**What starts the check.** On a Node.js server, `register` in `src/instrumentation.ts` calls `registerEventHandlers` and then `startScheduler`. `registerEventHandlers` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts` imports `notification-service`, and that import runs `registerFanOut`, which subscribes to `issue.overdue` before any tick. `startScheduler` in `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts` sets a 60-second interval. Each `tick` walks `CADENCE_MINUTES`. `overdue-issues` is due on the first tick and again 60 minutes after `lastRunAt`. A due kind is enqueued with id `overdue-issues:<minute>` and `drain` in `src/server/jobs/queue.ts` runs `runHandler`, which dynamically imports and calls `runOverdueIssueJob(now)`. The same function is also the only work of `POST` in `src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts`, after `assertCronSecret`. That route returns the job result and does not notify anyone.

**Which issues count.** `runOverdueIssueJob` in `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts` wraps the pass in `runJob("overdue-issues", …)`. It first calls `shouldFilterArchived({})` from `src/lib/soft-delete.ts`. An empty scope means “live rows only.” If that ever returned false, the sweep would log and exit. It then loads at most 50 org ids from `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup` (oldest `measuredAt` first) and, for each org, calls `issueRepo.listOverdueIssues(orgId, stamp)`. That query in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` keeps rows that are in the org, have `archivedAt` null, have a non-null `dueAt` strictly before `now`, and have status `backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, or `in_review`. `done` and `canceled` (`CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES` in `src/types/issue.ts`) never match. The job does not call `isOverdue` in `src/lib/date.ts`. That helper is the same comparison for the UI. Inside the loop the job also skips a null `dueAt`. It does not look at the assignee, preferences, or closed-ness again.

**What the job does and does not own.** For each remaining issue it `emit`s `issue.overdue` through `src/lib/event-bus.ts` with `orgId`, `actorId: null`, `occurredAt`, `issueId`, `projectId`, `dueAt`, and `assigneeId`. `emit` waits for every subscriber with `Promise.allSettled` and does not rethrow a handler failure. The job’s comment states the boundary: it only announces the fact. In-app rows, digest mail, and any other subscriber are someone else’s job. It does not render `OverdueEmail` or call `sendEmail`.

**Why the same issue is not announced on every pass.** A module-level `reported` set records issue ids for the life of the process. After a successful `emit`, the id is added and later sweeps `continue` when `reported.has(issue.id)`, even while the issue is still open and still past due. `resetOverdueTracking` clears that set for tests only. If `emit` throws, the id is not added, `result.failed` increments, and a later pass can try again. Because `emit` swallows handler rejections, a failed fan-out still counts as announced. The set is memory only, so a process restart can announce again. `enqueue` is idempotent per id, but each minute has a new id, so the scheduler does not provide the once-only guarantee. The set does.

**How one assignee hears about it.** The subscriber in `registerFanOut` (`src/server/services/notification-service.ts`) returns immediately when `assigneeId` is null. Otherwise it calls `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [assigneeId], …)` with title “An issue is overdue”, a body that names the issue and `dueAt`, href `/issues/${issueId}`, and `actorId: null`. `notify` loads the org for a `FlagContext`, then for each distinct recipient skips them only when they are `payload.actorId` (never, here, because the actor is null). It loads that user’s preference for `issue_overdue` via `preferenceRepo.getPreference` and passes it to `resolveChannels`. No stored preference means both `in_app` and `email`. A stored preference adds `in_app` only when `inApp` is set, and adds `email` when `email` is set and either `digestOnly` is false or the `digest_email` flag is on (`isEnabled`). An empty channel list writes no row. Otherwise `insertNotifications` stores one row whose `channels` are exactly that choice. Webhooks are not on this path: `registerWebhookListeners` does not subscribe to `issue.overdue`, and `resolveChannels` never adds `webhook`.

The in-app channel is that row. The dashboard shell and the inbox read it through `listNotifications` (`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx`, `inbox/page.tsx`, and the notifications panel).

The email channel on the row is not sent by this fan-out. Nothing in the overdue path calls `renderEmail("overdue")`. Mail goes out only for people who set `digestOnly` on at least one kind. `listDigestSubscribers` returns those users. On the org’s `digestHourUtc`, `runDigestEmailJob` calls `buildDigest`, which keeps their unread notifications in the last day (including this overdue row, capped by `DIGEST_MAX_ENTRIES`). `renderDigest` renders the `digest` template and `sendEmail` logs it to that user’s address (`userRepo.findUserById`). Each included notification is then `markRead`, so a later digest run in the same window does not send those entries again. `shouldRunForOrg` limits that job to the configured UTC hour, and the job also requires `digest_email`.
